title: About Dr. Gaby — Ometz Dental
subtitle: Twenty years of oral rehabilitation, operative and aesthetic dentistry. Written plans, honest second opinions, and clinical judgment. In Spanish and English, in Barrio Mburucuyá, Asunción.

sections.heading: Who she is
sections.body: I'm Dr. Gaby. I've been a dentist for two decades. It's not about grabbing the drill — it's about sitting down, listening to you, and building a treatment plan together that makes sense, that you understand, and that fits your needs. Oral rehabilitation, aesthetics, operative. I listen.

sections.heading: Practice phrase
sections.body: I listen. That's the foundation of everything.

sections.heading: How I work
items: I listen — the first consultation is to sit down and understand your case, not to sell you something.
I think before I touch — diagnosis, conversation, planning before any intervention.
I preserve before I replace — if a tooth can be restored, it is restored. If a crown is well made, it stays.
I explain until you understand — you decide with information, not fear.
I refer when appropriate — endodontics, orthodontics, surgery, implants: I refer to trusted colleagues.

sections.heading: The 3 specialties
items: Oral Rehabilitation — rebuilding mouths with history: accumulated treatment, failed procedures, complex cases. A plan, not patches.
Aesthetic Dentistry — bleaching, aesthetic restorations, with judgment (no veneers for 18-year-olds unless clinically indicated).
Operative Dentistry — caries restorations, composite resin, glass ionomer, ceromer. Material depends on the case.

sections.heading: How I think about a case
sections.body: When a patient says 'I want to replace this crown', I don't look only at the crown. I look at the substrate, the neighboring tooth, the age, the function, the occlusion, the endodontic history, the risk of touching a vital tooth, and the real expectation. When I see a broken molar, I don't ask only how to restore it. I ask whether it's vital, whether it's restorable, where the margin ends, how it will be isolated, what happens to adjacent teeth, and what the prognosis is. Treatment comes from a map, not an impulse.

sections.heading: The symbol: Ometz (אומץ — courage in Hebrew)
sections.body: Ometz means 'courage' in Hebrew. Courage to think before touching, to preserve before replacing, to explain before selling. And courage for patients who return to the chair after treatments that failed them: the courage to start again with judgment.

sections.heading: What the brand never says
sections.body: I don't sell no-prep veneers, guaranteed perfect smiles, unbeatable prices, risk-free treatment, or 'change your life in one appointment'. If you're 18 and want veneers, I won't do them. I'll explain why. What I do offer: 'before deciding, let's understand your case'. 'Not always the most visible treatment is the most indicated'. 'A good clinical decision can prevent many future problems'.

sections.heading: Outside the chair
sections.body: I'm 45. I spent 13 years at Odontología 3, and now I'm starting on my own. My scrubs are colorful. I have a lot of energy and my head is overwhelmed with 3000 ideas at the same time. I live in Luque. I speak English. I like books. I don't like community management. I'm opening Ometz Dental for patients who are tired of having procedures sold to them without the why being explained.

sections.heading: Training and practice
bullets: 20+ years in operative dentistry, aesthetic dentistry, and oral rehabilitation.
Volume: ~130 patients/month, 42 restorations in May 2026 alone.
Three real specialties: oral rehabilitation, aesthetics, operative.
Operational English for international patients (expats, medical tourism).
Dental coaching: teaches recently graduated dentists (differentiated service, doesn't exist in Paraguay yet).
Care: Monday to Friday, 2:30pm to 7:00pm, by appointment.
